programme: PPARD drives fatty-acid oxidation and directly targets PPARGC1A (PGC-1α), the master regulator of mitochondrial biogenesis; FOXO4 converges on the same node — PPARGC1A is independently listed among its targets — while also inducing the stress-resistance/antioxidant genes SOD2 and SIRT1; MAFG's target set (HMOX1, NQO1, NFE2L1) is the canonical NRF2-partner antioxidant-response-element signature. Together PPARD, FOXO4 and MAFG form a mitochondrial-biogenesis-plus-antioxidant-defense module that cells activate to buffer oxidative/metabolic stress.
role_in_a: In multiple sclerosis, PPARD constrains microglial reactivity and limits axonal injury through metabolic/mitochondrial support (direct experimental evidence: microglial PPARD loss worsens axonal damage). The NRF2-partner antioxidant arm this module represents (MAFG's HMOX1/NQO1 targets) is the same pathway that dimethyl fumarate, an approved oral MS therapy, is designed to activate, and FOXO4's SOD2/SIRT1/PPARGC1A targets fit the same redox-buffering, mitochondrial-quality-control logic needed to protect stressed axons and oligodendrocytes.
role_in_b: In endometrial carcinoma, this module would be expected to support tumor-cell metabolic adaptation: PPARD/PGC-1α-driven fatty-acid oxidation and NRF2-MAFG-driven antioxidant gene induction are mechanisms by which proliferating, hypoxic tumor cells buffer oxidative load and sustain growth — a pattern consistent with UCEC's well-established links to obesity, metabolic syndrome, and PI3K/AKT-driven lipid metabolism, though the retrieved record does not confirm this module specifically in UCEC tissue.
shared_axis: Both a chronically inflamed, oxidatively stressed CNS lesion in MS and a proliferating, metabolically demanding endometrial tumor in UCEC would benefit from the same PPARD/PGC-1α mitochondrial-biogenesis programme paired with a FOXO4/MAFG-NRF2 antioxidant arm, repurposed toward opposite ends — tissue protection in MS, cell survival under stress in the tumor.
reasoning: The module is nameable directly from the data (PPARD and FOXO4 both target PPARGC1A; MAFG's targets are the textbook NRF2-ARE signature) and PPARD carries genuine, disease-specific experimental support in MS at the highest concordance of any factor here (80/156). But only PPARD is placed by a citation, FOXO4 and MAFG have no disease-specific literature in the retrieved record, and the single UCEC-linked citation for PPARD is explicitly flagged as an unconfirmed pan-cancer mention rather than UCEC-specific data — so the connection to UCEC rests on established general biology (lipid metabolism/PI3K-AKT centrality in endometrial cancer) rather than retrieved evidence.
support: PMID 33732230 — direct experimental evidence that microglial PPARD deficiency exacerbates axonal injury in a demyelinating mouse model, supporting the metabolic/mitochondrial arm of this module in multiple sclerosis. PMID 33029111 — mentions PPARD within a broad pan-cancer analysis that includes UCEC, but per the reader's note the text does not confirm UCEC-specific findings, so this is weak, unconfirmed support only. No PMIDs in the material place FOXO4 or MAFG, or this module as a whole, in either disease.
how_to_falsify: Knock down or overexpress PPARD and MAFG in a UCEC cell line and measure PGC-1α induction, fatty-acid oxidation flux, NRF2-target expression (HMOX1, NQO1) and viability under oxidative/hypoxic stress; if neither factor moves these readouts or affects proliferation/survival, the module does not extend to UCEC and the shared-axis claim fails. In parallel, in the mouse MS model already showing a PPARD axonal-injury phenotype, additionally ablate FOXO4 in microglia or oligodendrocytes and test whether PPARGC1A induction and axonal protection are lost only when both factors are removed together; if FOXO4 loss adds nothing beyond the PPARD-only phenotype, the proposed convergence on PPARGC1A is not functionally real.
caveats: Tissue pairing is brain versus uterine endometrium — anatomically unrelated — and this account draws on only 3 independent cohort pairs underlying the 156 patient-group comparisons. Even among the chosen factors, concordance is partial, not universal: PPARD 80/156 (~51%), MAFG 67/156 (~43%), FOXO4 66/156 (~42%). ID4, REST, NR3C1 and SOX2 were removed as tissue-generic, which is why this account does not reach for a generic neural or steroid-hormone master regulator; ID2 and GLIS3 carry their own direct MS-specific citations (OPC differentiation, autoimmune-risk colocalization) but were left out of this programme because their target sets do not mechanistically connect to the PPARD/FOXO4/MAFG axis — including them would have produced a looser, harder-to-defend story. No factor here has any UCEC-specific citation in the retrieved material; the disease-B role is inference from established endometrial-cancer metabolic biology, not from retrieved evidence.
